newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU agrees tougher stance on Cuba - diplomats.
newsitem.headline: EU agrees tougher stance on Cuba - diplomats.

text.p: The European Union has agreed to toughen its stance towards Cuba and push Havana to respect human rights, free speech and freedom of association, diplomats said on Thursday.
The new policy, due for formal adoption on Monday, comes as Cuba has accused EU member Spain of meddling in its affairs and has withdrawn official approval for a new Spanish ambassador.

"The European Union will seek out opportunities -- even more actively than heretofore -- to remind the Cuban authorities, both publicly and privately, of fundamental responsibilities regarding human rights, in particular freedom of speech and association," an official EU policy paper says.
The 15-country EU also pledged to intensify talks with the Cuban authorities, and with all sectors of society, "to promote respect for human rights and real progress towards pluralist democracy".

European Union leaders have been under pressure from the United States to strengthen their stance towards Havana, which Washington hit with tougher economic sanctions this year after two U.S. civilian aircraft were shot down by Cuba in March.
"This will be a signal to Cuba and also to Washington that the EU is doing something on Cuba," one EU diplomat said of the new policy stance.

The United States and the European Union have repeatedly clashed on Cuba policy since the aircraft were downed, with Washington passing laws intended to punish foreign investors who "traffic" with nationalised properties on the island.
Under the Helms-Burton law, named for its sponsors, top executives and major shareholders of firms found to be "trafficking" are to be barred from the United States.
The U.S. says its citizens never received compensation for assets seized by Cuban President Fidel Castro since 1959, so it treats them as stolen properties.
The EU policy change makes clear its position on Helms-Burton remains unchanged.
"It is not EU policy to try to bring about change by coercive measures with the effect of increasing the economic hardship of the Cuban people," it said.
